tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

p='cli/src/doctor.ts'
s=open(p).read()
old_sig='function run(command: string, args: string[], opts: { cwd?: string; timeoutMs: number; signal: AbortSignal }): Promise'
new_sig='function run(command: string, args: string[], opts: { cwd?: string; timeoutMs: number; signal: AbortSignal; maxStdout?: number }): Promise'
assert s.count(old_sig)==1; s=s.replace(old_sig,new_sig)
old='stdout: stdout.slice(0, 64_000)'
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,'stdout: stdout.slice(0, opts.maxStdout ?? 64_000)')
old='''    const call = await run(binary, ["-w", workspace, "call", "--tool", "list_dir", "--args", JSON.stringify({ path: "." })], { timeoutMs: ctx.timeoutMs, signal });'''
new='''    // One level only, and the whole answer kept: a large workspace (a home directory) lists thousands of entries, and a
    // listing cut at the usual output cap would not parse and would look like an engine failure.

assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
The first `nexus doctor --deep` run (from `/home/mike`) failed one check, `engine.tool`. That was a bug in the doctor, not your setup. I fixed it, and a fresh `--deep` run now gives **20 pass, 0 warn, 0 fail, exit 0**.

**What went wrong:** with your home folder as the workspace, the engine's listing came to 6,715 entries (812 KB). The doctor keeps only the first 64 KB of a command's output. The cut-off output couldn't be read, so the doctor reported "could not execute a read-only tool" even though the engine had worked.

**Fix** (`cli/src/doctor.ts`): the probe now lists only the top level of the workspace and keeps up to 16 MB of output for that one call. A big workspace can no longer look like an engine failure.

**Verification:**
- I added a test with a workspace whose listing is bigger than the 64 KB limit. It reproduced the false failure before the fix and passes after.
- `make test`: Rust 192/192, CLI 716/716 (715 plus the new test), all security gates pass.
- The CLI is rebuilt and the doctor rerun from `/home/mike` is clean.

Every other check passed on the first run too, including the live inference request to `engine/b0`, which got a reply in 639 ms. I ran `--deep` a few times while checking the fix, and each run sends one short inference request to the model.

The changes to `doctor.ts`, `doctor.test.ts` and the rebuilt dist are not committed yet. Say if you want them committed to main.

<pasted_content id="ac96">
Improve Nexus’s live TUI diff output to a polished, readable standard. Implement and validate the actual terminal experience.

The visual references were reviewed separately and are unavailable on this development server. Their relevant qualities are specified below; no screenshot files are needed.

Read applicable AGENTS.md instructions, inspect the existing diff pipeline and TUI renderer, and preserve unrelated work. Reuse the current architecture.

Target presentation:
- A compact header such as `Edited cli/src/doctor.ts +4 −2`, with an identifiable path and accurate change counts.
- Consistent spacing between file operations and a subtle gutter defining each diff block.
- Muted green backgrounds spanning the visible width of added rows; muted red backgrounds for deleted rows; neutral unchanged context.
- Readable syntax highlighting within those backgrounds, with sufficient contrast.
- Explicit +/− markers so changes remain understandable without color.
- Aligned old/new line-number gutters, blank where a number does not apply.
- Preserved indentation, tabs, blank lines, and Unicode alignment.
- Clearly separated hunks with enough context to understand each edit.
- A bounded inline preview ending with an accurate omission message and discoverable review control, such as `… 48 more lines · <actual shortcut> to review`.

Behavior requirements:
1. Show each successful edit’s actual before/after diff in the transcript. Exclude unrelated pre-existing changes. Failed edits show an error and never appear successful.
2. Support additions, modifications, deletions, multiple hunks, repeated edits, and supported renames. Explain binary, oversized, unreadable, or unsupported changes accurately.
3. Provide a focused complete-diff view with file/hunk navigation and vertical/horizontal scrolling. Returning must preserve transcript position and composer text. Distinguish operation diffs from cumulative workspace/session diffs.
4. Handle narrow terminals, long paths and lines, resizing, and files without a final newline. Clipped content must remain inspectable. If the full diff cannot be retained, disclose the limit and provide a reliable retrieval path.
5. Escape terminal control sequences in file content without losing the represented meaning.
6. Keep activity indicators, steering, approvals, cancellation, and input usable while diffs arrive. Avoid flicker, duplicate entries, corrupted rows, unwanted scroll jumps, and unnecessary idle redraws.
7. Provide limited-color and monochrome fallbacks. State whether shell-command edits receive diff coverage.

Use shared rendering components and theme tokens. Resolve routine design decisions yourself and continue through implementation and validation.

Validate through the real TUI and sidecar in a pseudo-terminal:
- Mixed additions/deletions, multiple hunks, large diffs, long paths/lines, Unicode, tabs, blank lines, and missing final newlines.
- Failed edits and pre-existing dirty files.
- Wide and narrow layouts, including resizing during active editing.
- Complete-diff navigation, draft preservation, and return to the transcript.
- Meaningful regression checks for accuracy, alignment, clipping, terminal escaping, and duplicate events.

Run required builds and relevant tests. Capture representative terminal screenshots and a recording with monotonic timestamps, tied to the tested commit/build. Inspect the rendered output independently for hierarchy, readability, alignment, contrast, density, and navigation; correct visible shortcomings before declaring completion.

Deliver the changes, tested commit/build identity, screenshots, tests actually run, supported cases, remaining limitations, and a clear visual acceptance verdict. Do not publish or deploy.
</pasted_content id="ac96">

lines: /** Unified diff of the operation (headers `--- a/` `+++ b/`), or empty when line detail is unavailable. */
/** Why there is no line detail, when there is none. */
+ * Lines compared by the diff. A last line without a final newline is kept distinct from the same text with one (the
+ * sentinel never occurs in text), so adding or removing only the final newline is a change, as in git.
+/** A diff row for `op`, followed by git's marker when its line is the last one of a file without a final newline. */
+  return [`${op.kind}${op.line.slice(0, -NO_EOL.length)}`, "\\ No newline at end of file"];
/** Myers O(ND) shortest edit script over lines. */
function diffLines(a: string[], b: string[]): Op[] {
-  if (noNewline(oldText) !== noNewline(newText) && hunks.length) hunks.push("\\ No newline at end of file (one side)");
-  return { kind, added, removed, diff: hunks.length ? [...header, ...hunks].join("\n") : "" };
+  return { kind, added, removed, hunks: hunkCount, diff: hunks.length ? [...header, ...hunks].join("\n") : "" };
+/** Changed and context lines of a unified diff: what "N more lines" counts (headers and markers are not lines). */
/** At most `maxLines` lines / `maxChars` characters of a diff, and whether it was cut. */
export function previewDiff(diff: string, maxLines = 40, maxChars = 6000): { preview: string; truncated: boolean; totalLines: number } {
return { preview: out, truncated: count < lines.length, totalLines: lines.length };
+ * File content made safe to print without losing what it says: C0 controls (except tab and newline) become their
+ * Unicode control pictures (ESC is `␛`, CR is `␍`), DEL becomes `␡`, and C1 controls and bidirectional overrides
+ * (which reorder what a terminal shows) become `<U+XXXX>`. A terminal never receives a control sequence from a diff.

        total_lines: u64,
        #[serde(default)]
        note: Option<String>,

        diff_lines: Option<u64>,
        #[serde(default)]
        hunks: Option<u64>,
        /// The complete diff on disk.
        #[serde(default)]
        full_path: Option<String>,
        #[serde(default)]
        note: Option<String>,
    },''')
rep('''        /// Full diff of the file change the call made.
        #[serde(default)]
        diff: Option<String>,
    },''','''        /// Full diff of the file change the call made (cut to the sidecar's in-memory limit).
        #[serde(default)]
        diff: Option<String>,
        /// Characters in the complete diff, and where it is on disk.
        #[serde(default)]
        diff_chars: Option<u64>,
        #[serde(default)]
        diff_path: Option<String>,
    },''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

def squeezed(self, since=0):
        """Screen text without whitespace: cells that did not change are skipped with cursor moves, not spaces."""
        return re.sub(r"\s", "", self.screen_text(since))

    def wait_text(self, text, timeout):
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        text = re.sub(r"\s", "", text)
        while text not in self.squeezed():
            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                raise TimeoutError(f"never saw {text!r}; tail: {self.screen_text()[-1500:]!r}")
            self.pump(0.1)

    def wait_idle(self, timeout=20):
        """Until the idle hint is on screen: the sidecar reported the turn over (typing earlier would steer)."""
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while not any("enter send" in line for line in self.screen.lines()):
            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                raise TimeoutError(f"never idle; screen: {self.screen.text()!r}")
            self.pump(0.05)

    def alive(self):
        try:
            pid, _ = os.waitpid(self.pid, os.WNOHANG)
            return pid == 0
        except ChildProcessError:
            return False

    def wait_exit(self, timeout):
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            self.pump(0.1)
            try:
                pid, status = os.waitpid(self.pid, os.WNOHANG)
            except ChildProcessError:
                return None
            if pid:
                return os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
        return "timeout"


def tui_pid(session_pid):
    """The pty child execs nexus-tui directly, so its pid is the TUI's."""
    return session_pid


def count_events(path, kind):
    try:
        with open(path) as f:
            return sum(1 for line in f if f'"type":"{kind}"' in line)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return 0


def wait_events(path, kind, count, timeout, session):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while count_events(path, kind) < count:
        if time.monotonic() > deadline:
            raise TimeoutError(f"expected {count} {kind} events; tail: {session.screen_text()[-1500:]!r}")
        session.pump(0.1)


def main():
    plan = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
    env = dict(os.environ, **plan["env"])
    cast = []
    result = {"steps": []}
    events = plan["env"]["NEXUS_RECORD_EVENTS"]
    argv = [plan["tui"], "--live", "--sidecar", plan["recorder"], "--node", plan["node"], "--"] + plan["sidecar_args"]

    s = Session(argv, env, 120, 40, cast)
    s.wait_text("enter send", 30)
    s.pump(0.3)

    # 1. A slow inference step: the indicator animates with no model output arriving.
    s.send("Edit notes.txt, then write the batch files f4 to f34.\r", settle=0.1)
    mark = len(s.out)
    cpu0, t0 = cpu_seconds(s.pid), time.monotonic()
    s.pump(0.8)
    # 2. Steering while the agent works (Enter while busy sends steering, not a second prompt).
    snapshot_a = s.screen.text()
    s.send("keep line 1 unchanged\r", settle=0.1)
    s.pump(0.6)
    snapshot_b = s.screen.text()
    s.pump(0.3)
    busy_cpu = (cpu_seconds(s.pid) - cpu0) / (time.monotonic() - t0)
    window = s.squeezed(mark)
    frames = sorted({c for c in window if c in SPINNER})
    result["slow_inference"] = {
        "spinner_frames_seen": frames,
        "thinking_shown": "thinking · 0:0" in snapshot_a,
        "elapsed_shown": bool(re.search(r"thinking · 0:0[1-9]", snapshot_b)),
        "busy_line": next((l for l in snapshot_b.split("\n") if "thinking" in l), ""),
        "status_line": snapshot_b.split("\n")[0],
        "busy_cpu_fraction": round(busy_cpu, 4),
        "steering_echoed": "↳keepline1unchanged" in window,
    }

    # 3. The long turn: edits (one failing), then more than 30 steps, continuing without the operator.
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 1, 90, s)
    s.pump(0.5)
    whole = s.squeezed()
    result["long_turn"] = {
        "diff_shown": "Editednotes.txt+1−1" in whole,
        "diff_lines_shown": "−line2" in whole and "+linetwo" in whole,
        "failed_edit_marked": "×" in whole,
        "steering_applied_shown": "steering·applied" in whole,
        "segment_2_shown": "segment2" in whole,
    }

    # 4. Idle: no redraws and next to no CPU while nothing happens.
    s.pump(0.5)
    before = len(s.raw)
    cpu0, t0 = cpu_seconds(s.pid), time.monotonic()
    s.pump(3.0)
    result["idle"] = {
        "bytes_written": len(s.raw) - before,
        "cpu_fraction": round((cpu_seconds(s.pid) - cpu0) / (time.monotonic() - t0), 4),
    }

    composer_rows = []

        before = len(s.raw)
        s.set_size(cols, rows)
        s.pump(0.6)
        redraws.append(len(s.raw) - before)
        composer_rows.append(any("enter send" in line for line in s.screen.lines()))
    result["resize"] = {"redraw_bytes": redraws, "alive": s.alive(), "hint_visible_after_each": composer_rows, "last_frame_rows": len(s.screen.lines())}

    s.wait_idle()
    # 6. A multi-line bracketed paste: one buffer, shown compactly, submitted exactly; "/exit" inside is data.
    mark = len(s.out)
    s.send("\x1b[200~first line\r\n/exit\r\n  indented ünïcødé\x1b[201~", settle=0.4)
    result["paste"] = {"label_shown": "[Pastedtext#1:3lines]" in s.squeezed(mark)}
    s.send("\r", settle=0.2)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 2, 30, s)
    result["paste"]["alive_after"] = s.alive()
    s.wait_idle()

    # 7. Cancellation during a slow step: Esc cancels; the indicator stops.
    s.send("take your time\r", settle=0.1)
    s.pump(1.5)
    # Resize while busy: the animated frame keeps going at the new size.
    s.set_size(90, 30)
    s.pump(0.5)
    result["resize_busy"] = any("thinking" in line for line in s.screen.lines())
    s.set_size(120, 40)
    s.pump(0.3)
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.1)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 3, 30, s)
    s.pump(0.6)
    before = len(s.raw)
    s.pump(1.5)
    result["cancel"] = {"bytes_after_settle": len(s.raw) - before, "idle_hint_back": any("enter send" in line for line in s.screen.lines())}

    # 8. Quit cleanly (ctrl-c on an idle, empty composer), then resume the saved session in a new TUI.
    s.send("\x03", settle=0.1)
    result["first_exit"] = s.wait_exit(20)
    cast.append([round(time.monotonic() - T0, 4), "m", "second TUI process: resume the saved session (-r latest)"])
    r = Session(argv + ["-r", "latest"], env, 100, 30, cast)
    r.wait_text("Resumed session", 30)
    r.wait_idle()
    r.send("are you still there?\r", settle=0.2)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 4, 30, r)
    r.pump(0.3)
    r.send("\x03", settle=0.1)
    result["second_exit"] = r.wait_exit(20)
    result["resumed_shown"] = "Resumedsession" in r.squeezed()

    times = [frame[0] for frame in cast]
    result["recording"] = {

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Drives the real `nexus-tui --live` binary (with the real sidecar) through edits whose diffs must render well:
mixed additions and deletions, several hunks, a repeated edit, a failed edit, an addition, a deletion, a long path
with a long line and wide characters, a file without a final newline, a large change and terminal escapes in file
content. It resizes while the edits arrive, steers while busy, opens the full-diff review with a draft in the
composer, runs `/diff`, and repeats one edit at 256-colour, 16-colour and monochrome depth.

It keeps a colour-aware model of the screen (SGR colours and attributes, wide characters) so the node test can check
alignment and colour, and it writes the screens it was asked to capture as JSON (rendered to PNG separately by
render_screens.py). The node test (tui_diff_e2e.test.ts) owns the mock gateway and checks the sidecar logs.

Usage: tui_diff_driver.py PLAN.json
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
import unicodedata

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from tui_pty_driver import T0, Session, count_events, wait_events  # noqa: E402

DEFAULT = None


def char_width(ch):
    if unicodedata.combining(ch) or unicodedata.category(ch) in ("Mn", "Me", "Cf"):
        return 0
    return 2 if unicodedata.east_asian_width(ch) in ("W", "F") else 1


class ColorScreen:
    """A terminal model that keeps each cell's character, colours and attributes: cursor positioning, erase, SGR."""

    TOKEN = re.compile(r"\x1b\[([0-9;?<>=:]*)([ -/]*)([@-~])|\x1b\][^\x07\x1b]*(?:\x07|\x1b\\)|\x1b[()][0-9A-Za-z]|\x1b[=>78DEHM]|([\r\n\b])|([^\x1b\r\n\b]+)")

    def __init__(self, cols, rows):
        self.resize(cols, rows)

    def blank(self):
        return [" ", DEFAULT, DEFAULT, 0]

    def resize(self, cols, rows):
        self.cols, self.rows = cols, rows
        self.grid = [[self.blank() for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]
        self.row = self.col = 0
        self.fg = self.bg = DEFAULT
        self.attrs = 0  # bit 1 bold, 2 dim, 4 italic, 8 reverse

    def sgr(self, params):
        nums = [int(n) if n.isdigit() else 0 for n in params.replace(":", ";").split(";")] if params else [0]
        i = 0
        while i < len(nums):
            n = nums[i]
            if n == 0:
                self.fg = self.bg = DEFAULT
                self.attrs = 0
            elif n == 1:
                self.attrs |= 1
            elif n == 2:
                self.attrs |= 2
            elif n == 3:
                self.attrs |= 4
            elif n == 7:
                self.attrs |= 8
            elif n == 22:
                self.attrs &= ~3
            elif n == 23:
                self.attrs &= ~4
            elif n == 27:
                self.attrs &= ~8
            elif 30 <= n <= 37 or 90 <= n <= 97:
                self.fg = ["ansi", n - 30 if n < 90 else n - 90 + 8]
            elif 40 <= n <= 47 or 100 <= n <= 107:
                self.bg = ["ansi", n - 40 if n < 100 else n - 100 + 8]
            elif n == 39:
                self.fg = DEFAULT
            elif n == 49:
                self.bg = DEFAULT
            elif n in (38, 48) and i + 1 < len(nums):
                if nums[i + 1] == 5 and i + 2 < len(nums):
                    value = ["idx", nums[i + 2]]
                    i += 2
                elif nums[i + 1] == 2 and i + 4 < len(nums):
                    value = ["rgb", nums[i + 2], nums[i + 3], nums[i + 4]]
                    i += 4
                else:
                    value = DEFAULT
                if n == 38:
                    self.fg = value
                else:
                    self.bg = value
                i += 1
            i += 1

    def put(self, ch):
        width = char_width(ch)
        if width == 0:
            if self.col > 0:
                self.grid[self.row][self.col - 1][0] += ch
            return
        if self.col + width > self.cols:
            return
        self.grid[self.row][self.col] = [ch, self.fg, self.bg, self.attrs]
        if width == 2 and self.col + 1 < self.cols:
            self.grid[self.row][self.col + 1] = ["", self.fg, self.bg, self.attrs]
        self.col += width

    def feed(self, text):
        for m in self.TOKEN.finditer(text):
            params, _, final, ctl, chars = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3), m.group(4), m.group(5)
            if final:
                if final == "m":
                    self.sgr(params)
                    continue
                nums = [int(n) if n.isdigit() else 0 for n in params.lstrip("?").split(";")] if params else []
                if final in "Hf":
                    self.row = max(0, min(self.rows - 1, (nums[0] if nums and nums[0] else 1) - 1))
                    self.col = max(0, min(self.cols - 1, (nums[1] if len(nums) > 1 and nums[1] else 1) - 1))
                elif final == "J" and (not nums or nums[0] in (2, 3)):
                    self.grid = [[self.blank() for _ in range(self.cols)] for _ in range(self.rows)]
                elif final == "K":
                    mode = nums[0] if nums else 0
                    span = range(self.col, self.cols) if mode == 0 else range(0, self.col + 1) if mode == 1 else range(self.cols)
                    for c in span:
                        self.grid[self.row][c] = [" ", DEFAULT, self.bg, 0]
                elif final == "C":
                    self.col = min(self.cols - 1, self.col + (nums[0] if nums and nums[0] else 1))
                elif final == "D":
                    self.col = max(0, self.col - (nums[0] if nums and nums[0] else 1))
                elif final == "G":
                    self.col = max(0, min(self.cols - 1, (nums[0] if nums and nums[0] else 1) - 1))
            elif ctl == "\r":
                self.col = 0
            elif ctl == "\n":
                self.row = min(self.rows - 1, self.row + 1)
            elif ctl == "\b":
                self.col = max(0, self.col - 1)
            elif chars:
                for ch in chars:
                    if ord(ch) < 32:
                        continue
                    self.put(ch)

    def lines(self):
        return ["".join(cell[0] for cell in row).rstrip() for row in self.grid]

    def snapshot(self, name):
        return {"name": name, "cols": self.cols, "rows": self.rows, "at": round(time.monotonic() - T0, 4), "cells": [[list(c) for c in row] for row in self.grid]}


class DiffSession(Session):
    """A Session that also feeds the colour-aware screen."""

    def __init__(self, argv, env, cols, rows, cast):
        self.color = ColorScreen(cols, rows)
        super().__init__(argv, env, cols, rows, cast)

    def set_size(self, cols, rows, signal_child=True):
        if hasattr(self, "color"):
            self.color.resize(cols, rows)
        super().set_size(cols, rows, signal_child)

    def pump(self, seconds):
        got = super().pump(seconds)
        if got:
            self.color.feed(got.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        return got

    def wait_screen(self, predicate, timeout, what):
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while not predicate(self.color.lines()):
            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                raise TimeoutError(f"never saw {what}; screen:\n" + "\n".join(self.color.lines()))
            self.pump(0.05)


def has(lines, text):
    squeezed = re.sub(r"\s", "", text)
    return any(squeezed in re.sub(r"\s", "", line) for line in lines)


def main():
    plan = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
    env = dict(os.environ, **plan["env"])
    events = plan["env"]["NEXUS_RECORD_EVENTS"]
    cast = []
    shots = []
    result = {}
    argv = [plan["tui"], "--live", "--sidecar", plan["recorder"], "--node", plan["node"], "--"] + plan["sidecar_args"]

    s = DiffSession(argv, env, 120, 40, cast)
    s.wait_text("enter send", 30)
    s.pump(0.3)
    s.send("Apply the review fixes across the repository.\r", settle=0.1)

    # While the edits arrive: capture the first card, resize narrow mid-turn, steer, then resize back.
    wait_events(events, "file.diff", 1, 30, s)
    s.pump(0.4)
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("01-first-edit-wide-active"))
    wait_events(events, "file.diff", 2, 30, s)
    s.set_size(72, 30)
    s.pump(0.6)
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("02-narrow-during-editing"))
    result["narrow_rows_within_width"] = all(len(line) <= 72 for line in s.color.lines())
    s.send("keep the public API stable\r", settle=0.2)
    wait_events(events, "file.diff", 5, 40, s)
    s.set_size(120, 40)
    s.pump(0.6)
    result["busy_after_resize"] = has(s.color.lines(), "esc to cancel")
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 1, 90, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    s.pump(0.5)
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("03-turn-complete-wide"))

    # Idle: nothing is redrawn while nothing happens.
    before = len(s.raw)
    s.pump(2.5)
    result["idle_bytes"] = len(s.raw) - before

    # Scroll back through the transcript, one page at a time, capturing what the operator sees.
    pages = []
    for i in range(6):
        pages.append(s.color.lines())
        s.send("\x1b[5~", settle=0.3)  # PageUp
    for i in range(3):
        shots.append(s.color.snapshot(f"04-scrollback-{i + 1}")) if i == 0 else None
    result["scrollback_pages"] = pages
    s.send("\x1b[6~" * 10, settle=0.4)  # back to the newest

    # The complete diff: a draft in the composer, ctrl+d, navigate, return.
    s.send("draft: compare with the spec", settle=0.3)
    s.pump(0.3)
    transcript_before = s.color.lines()[1:-3]
    s.send("\x04", settle=0.6)  # ctrl+d
    s.wait_screen(lambda lines: has(lines, "Edit diff · this operation only") and not has(lines, "Loading the complete diff"), 10, "the review panel")
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("05-review-newest-edit"))
    result["review_newest"] = s.color.lines()
    # Back through the edits to the multi-hunk one.
    target = None
    for _ in range(12):
        s.send("[", settle=0.5)
        s.wait_screen(lambda lines: not has(lines, "Loading the complete diff"), 10, "the previous edit")
        if has(s.color.lines(), "Editedsrc/app.ts") and has(s.color.lines(), "edit1of"):
            target = s.color.lines()
            break
    result["review_first_edit"] = target or s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("06-review-multi-hunk"))
    s.send("n", settle=0.4)
    result["review_after_n"] = s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("07-review-next-hunk"))
    # The long-path edit: pan right, then wrap.
    for _ in range(12):
        s.send("]", settle=0.5)
        s.wait_screen(lambda lines: not has(lines, "Loading the complete diff"), 10, "the next edit")
        if has(s.color.lines(), "configuration_loader.rs"):
            break
    result["review_long_clipped"] = s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("08-review-long-line-clipped"))
    s.send("\x1b[C" * 30, settle=0.5)
    result["review_long_panned"] = s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("09-review-long-line-panned"))
    s.send("w", settle=0.5)
    result["review_long_wrapped"] = s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("10-review-long-line-wrapped"))
    s.set_size(72, 30)
    s.pump(0.6)
    result["review_narrow"] = s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("11-review-narrow"))
    s.set_size(120, 40)
    s.pump(0.6)
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.6)  # esc: back to the transcript
    s.pump(0.3)
    result["after_review"] = {
        "draft_kept": has(s.color.lines()[-2:], "draft: compare with the spec"),
        "transcript_restored": s.color.lines()[1:-3] == transcript_before,
        "panel_closed": not has(s.color.lines(), "Edit diff · this operation only"),
    }
    # Clear the draft, then the cumulative workspace diff.
    s.send("\x0c", settle=0.3)  # ctrl+l clears the draft
    s.send("/diff\r", settle=0.3)
    s.wait_screen(lambda lines: has(lines, "Cumulative workspace diff"), 15, "the workspace diff")
    s.pump(0.4)
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("12-workspace-diff-transcript"))
    result["workspace_transcript"] = s.color.lines()
    s.send("\x04", settle=0.6)
    s.wait_screen(lambda lines: has(lines, "Workspace diff · all uncommitted changes"), 10, "the workspace review")
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("13-workspace-review"))
    result["workspace_review"] = s.color.lines()
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.4)
    s.send("\x03", settle=0.1)

        super().set_size(cols, rows, signal_child)

    def pump(self, seconds):
        got = super().pump(seconds)
        if got:
            self.color.feed(got.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        return got

    def wait_screen(self, predicate, timeout, what):
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while not predicate(self.color.lines()):
            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                raise TimeoutError(f"never saw {what}; screen:\n" + "\n".join(self.color.lines()))
            self.pump(0.05)


def has(lines, text):
    squeezed = re.sub(r"\s", "", text)
    return any(squeezed in re.sub(r"\s", "", line) for line in lines)


def main():
    plan = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
    env = dict(os.environ, **plan["env"])
    events = plan["env"]["NEXUS_RECORD_EVENTS"]
    cast = []
    shots = []
    result = {}
    argv = [plan["tui"], "--live", "--sidecar", plan["recorder"], "--node", plan["node"], "--"] + plan["sidecar_args"]

    s = DiffSession(argv, env, 120, 40, cast)
    s.wait_text("enter send", 30)
    s.pump(0.3)
    s.send("Apply the review fixes across the repository.\r", settle=0.1)

    # While the edits arrive: capture the first card, resize narrow mid-turn, steer, then resize back.
    wait_events(events, "file.diff", 1, 30, s)
    s.pump(0.4)
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("01-first-edit-wide-active"))
    wait_events(events, "file.diff", 2, 30, s)
    s.set_size(72, 30)
    s.pump(0.6)
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("02-narrow-during-editing"))
    result["narrow_rows_within_width"] = all(len(line) <= 72 for line in s.color.lines())
    s.send("keep the public API stable\r", settle=0.2)
    wait_events(events, "file.diff", 5, 40, s)
    s.set_size(120, 40)
    s.pump(0.6)
    result["busy_after_resize"] = has(s.color.lines(), "esc to cancel")
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 1, 90, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    s.pump(0.5)
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("03-turn-complete-wide"))

    # Idle: nothing is redrawn while nothing happens.
    before = len(s.raw)
    s.pump(2.5)
    result["idle_bytes"] = len(s.raw) - before

    # Scroll back through the transcript, one page at a time, capturing what the operator sees.
    pages = []
    for i in range(6):
        pages.append(s.color.lines())
        s.send("\x1b[5~", settle=0.3)  # PageUp
    for i in range(3):
        shots.append(s.color.snapshot(f"04-scrollback-{i + 1}")) if i == 0 else None
    result["scrollback_pages"] = pages
    s.send("\x1b[6~" * 10, settle=0.4)  # back to the newest

    # The complete diff: a draft in the composer, ctrl+d, navigate, return.
    s.send("draft: compare with the spec", settle=0.3)
    s.pump(0.3)
    transcript_before = s.color.lines()[1:-3]
    s.send("\x04", settle=0.6)  # ctrl+d
    s.wait_screen(lambda lines: has(lines, "Edit diff · this operation only") and not has(lines, "Loading the complete diff"), 10, "the review panel")
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("05-review-newest-edit"))
    result["review_newest"] = s.color.lines()
    # Back through the edits to the multi-hunk one.
    target = None
    for _ in range(12):
        s.send("[", settle=0.5)
        s.wait_screen(lambda lines: not has(lines, "Loading the complete diff"), 10, "the previous edit")
        if has(s.color.lines(), "Editedsrc/app.ts") and has(s.color.lines(), "edit1of"):
            target = s.color.lines()
            break
    result["review_first_edit"] = target or s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("06-review-multi-hunk"))
    s.send("n", settle=0.4)
    result["review_after_n"] = s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("07-review-next-hunk"))
    # The long-path edit: pan right, then wrap.
    for _ in range(12):
        s.send("]", settle=0.5)
        s.wait_screen(lambda lines: not has(lines, "Loading the complete diff"), 10, "the next edit")
        if has(s.color.lines(), "configuration_loader.rs"):
            break
    result["review_long_clipped"] = s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("08-review-long-line-clipped"))
    s.send("\x1b[C" * 30, settle=0.5)
    result["review_long_panned"] = s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("09-review-long-line-panned"))
    s.send("w", settle=0.5)
    result["review_long_wrapped"] = s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("10-review-long-line-wrapped"))
    s.set_size(72, 30)
    s.pump(0.6)
    result["review_narrow"] = s.color.lines()
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("11-review-narrow"))
    s.set_size(120, 40)
    s.pump(0.6)
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.6)  # esc: back to the transcript
    s.pump(0.3)
    result["after_review"] = {
        "draft_kept": has(s.color.lines()[-2:], "draft: compare with the spec"),
        "transcript_restored": s.color.lines()[1:-3] == transcript_before,
        "panel_closed": not has(s.color.lines(), "Edit diff · this operation only"),
    }
    # Clear the draft, then the cumulative workspace diff.
    s.send("\x0c", settle=0.3)  # ctrl+l clears the draft
    s.send("/diff\r", settle=0.3)
    s.wait_screen(lambda lines: has(lines, "Cumulative workspace diff"), 15, "the workspace diff")
    s.pump(0.4)
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("12-workspace-diff-transcript"))
    result["workspace_transcript"] = s.color.lines()
    s.send("\x04", settle=0.6)
    s.wait_screen(lambda lines: has(lines, "Workspace diff · all uncommitted changes"), 10, "the workspace review")
    shots.append(s.color.snapshot("13-workspace-review"))
    result["workspace_review"] = s.color.lines()
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.4)
    s.send("\x03", settle=0.1)
    result["first_exit"] = s.wait_exit(20)
    result["main_raw_has_osc52"] = "\x1b]52;" in s.raw.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    result["main_raw_has_clear_from_file"] = "␛[2J" not in s.raw.decode("utf-8", "replace") and False

    # The same small edit at lower colour depths.
    depths = {}
    for name, extra in plan["depth_sessions"]:
        cast.append([round(time.monotonic() - T0, 4), "m", f"new TUI process: {name}"])
        session_env = dict(env, **extra)
        if "COLORTERM" not in extra:
            session_env.pop("COLORTERM", None)
        d = DiffSession(argv, session_env, 100, 24, cast)
        d.wait_text("enter send", 30)
        d.pump(0.3)
        done = count_events(events, "turn.result")
        d.send("make the small edit\r", settle=0.2)
        wait_events(events, "turn.result", done + 1, 40, d)
        d.wait_idle()
        d.pump(0.4)
        shots.append(d.color.snapshot(f"14-depth-{name}"))
        depths[name] = {"lines": d.color.lines(), "cells": d.color.snapshot(name)["cells"]}
        d.send("\x03", settle=0.1)
        d.wait_exit(20)
    result["depths"] = depths

    times = [frame[0] for frame in cast]
    result["recording"] = {"frames": len(cast), "monotonic": all(b >= a for a, b in zip(times, times[1:])), "duration_s": times[-1] if times else 0}
    with open(plan["cast"], "w") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({"version": 2, "width": 120, "height": 40, "timestamp": int(time.time()), "env": {"TERM": env.get("TERM", "")}}) + "\n")
        for frame in cast:
            f.write(json.dumps(frame) + "\n")
    with open(plan["screens"], "w") as f:
        json.dump(shots, f)
    result["main_screens"] = {shot["name"]: ColorScreenLines(shot) for shot in shots}
    print(json.dumps(result))


def ColorScreenLines(shot):  # noqa: N802 — a projection used only for the summary
    return ["".join(cell[0] for cell in row).rstrip() for row in shot["cells"]]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

- **Activity line.** While the agent works, the line above the composer animates (`⠋ thinking · 0:42 · step 31 ·
  segment 2`) from the clock, not from model output, and names the phase: thinking, the running tool and its subject,
  waiting for the provider, verifying, compacting. It stops on completion, cancellation, failure or disconnection;
  an approval request replaces it with the approval hint.
- **Steering.** Enter while the agent works sends the draft as steering. It shows in the transcript as
  `↳ text · steering · queued`, then `applied` once the agent takes it at its next step. Steering that arrives as
  the turn finishes starts a follow-up turn; steering that cannot be applied (the turn was cancelled, a command was
  running, the agent stopped) is put back into the composer. Slash commands wait for idle, except read-only `/doctor`,
  `/help` and `/receipt`.
- **Paste buffers.** A multi-line or long paste becomes `[Pasted text #1: 24 lines]` in the composer; its content is
  submitted exactly as pasted (newlines in it never send, and a pasted `/exit` is text). Ctrl+O shows a buffer,
  Ctrl+X turns it back into editable text, Backspace after it removes it. Terminals without bracketed paste: a burst
  of keys with a line break inside it is treated as a paste.
- **File diffs.** Each successful edit shows that operation's own diff under its tool line (`± src/a.ts modified +3
  -1`, a bounded preview); pre-existing uncommitted changes are never attributed to the agent, and failed edits show
  none. Tab, `[`/`]` to select it, Enter opens the full diff.

`--max-steps` (default 30) is now a segment: at each segment boundary the turn checkpoints and continues on its own
while it makes progress. It stops with a stated reason on `--max-total-steps` (300), `--max-turn-minutes` (120),
`--stagnation-steps` without progress (12), a repeated identical action after two recovery notes, cancellation, or
the model finishing. `--no-continuation` restores the old single-segment turn. The operator's objective and its

requirement progress with evidence, and a turn that stops with requirements open ends `REQUIREMENTS_INCOMPLETE`

requirement the agent marks descoped stays unresolved until you run `/requirements accept <id>` (`/requirements`

python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p='src/bin/nexus_tui/sidecar.rs'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''pub enum SidecarMsg {
    Event(Event),''','''pub enum SidecarMsg {
    /// Boxed: events are large and the other messages carry nothing.
    Event(Box<Event>),''')
s=s.replace('parse_event(&line).map_or(SidecarMsg::Malformed, SidecarMsg::Event)','parse_event(&line).map_or(SidecarMsg::Malformed, |event| SidecarMsg::Event(Box::new(event)))')
# matches!(x, SidecarMsg::Event(Event::Hello { ... })) -> matches!(x, SidecarMsg::Event(e) if matches!(*e, Event::Hello { ... }))
s=re.sub(r'SidecarMsg::Event\((Event::Hello \{[^}]*\})\)\n', lambda m: 'SidecarMsg::Event(event) if matches!(*event, '+m.group(1)+')\n', s)
s=s.replace('''            SidecarMsg::Event(Event::SessionState { model, busy, .. }) => {''','''            SidecarMsg::Event(event) if matches!(*event, Event::SessionState { .. }) => {
                let Event::SessionState { model, busy, .. } = *event else { unreachable!() };''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='src/bin/nexus_tui/live.rs'
s=open(p).read()
old='''                SidecarMsg::Event(event) => {
                    self.state.apply(event);'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,'''                SidecarMsg::Event(event) => {
                    self.state.apply(*event);''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

feat(tui): readable per-operation diffs, full-diff review and colour fallbacks

Edit cards replace the plain tool row for successful file edits: a compact
`✓ Edited path +a −r` heading, then up to 14 diff lines in a gutter-marked block
with aligned old/new line numbers, explicit +/− markers, syntax colours on muted
full-width green/red rows, tab stops, hunk gaps and exact omission counts that
name the review control. One shared component (diff_view.rs) renders cards, the
workspace /diff output and the new review panel (ctrl+d / enter): hunk and
edit/file navigation, vertical scrolling, horizontal panning with ‹ › markers,
wrap toggle; returning keeps the transcript position and the draft.

Accuracy and safety: git-exact "\ No newline at end of file" markers; control
characters in file content shown as visible stand-ins instead of stripped;
diff_lines/hunks counts on file.diff; each operation's complete redacted diff
kept in ~/.nexus/sessions/<session>.diffs/ and served after the in-memory record
is cut or dropped; failed edits never carry a diff; repeated events replace
their card; the transcript stays anchored while content arrives below a
scrolled-back window.

Colour depth is detected (COLORTERM, TERM, NO_COLOR, NEXUS_COLOR) and every
frame is downsampled to 256/16 colours or monochrome; diff palettes are chosen
per depth with a WCAG 4.5:1 contrast test.

Validated through the real TUI and sidecar in a PTY (tui_diff_e2e.test.ts).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

input.content:
# Live TUI diff output — implementation and validation (2026-10-12)

Request: bring the live TUI's diff output to a polished, readable standard, validated through the real TUI and
sidecar in a pseudo-terminal. Code commit: `35ef104` on branch `feat/tui-diff-review` (not merged, not published).

## Tested build

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Commit | `35ef1043657d16a50e3c7fdd417d5ce2ab990818` (evidence run from a clean worktree of this commit) |
| `nexus-tui` SHA-256 | `a4441deba83b68701e2e13a7fad8d8b506dbcc4429b99b86ddf05fae4e6d6b40` |
| `cli/dist/sidecar.js` SHA-256 | `5765afd168a744f5081ed56dda77fdcc12f1eab5906a14ea4895e8a9bb4bae1e` |
| Evidence run | `894fe0f9-f2b2-4f26-aa7d-052f8f24d359`, 2026-10-12T05:13:22Z, recording 163 frames over 32.8 s, timestamps monotonic |
| Evidence | `docs/reviews/evidence/tui_diff/` — `tui_diff.cast` (asciicast v2), `tui_diff_screens.json` (captured cells with colours), `screens/*.png` (16 screenshots rendered from those cells), `tui_diff.metrics.json`, `SHA256SUMS` |

The PNGs are rendered by `cli/test/helpers/render_screens.py` (Pillow, a local evidence tool, not a dependency) from
the colour-aware screen model in `cli/test/helpers/tui_diff_driver.py`. Small glyphs for control pictures (`␛`, `␇`)
and CJK come from the renderer's fallback fonts; the TUI's own output is in the recording.

## What changed

- **Shared component** `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/diff_view.rs`: unified-diff parser (git and sidecar formats, hunk
  bodies read by count, renames, binary, deleted/new files, `\ No newline`, cut markers), row layout at the exact
  drawing width (indent, gutter bar, aligned old/new numbers blank where not applicable, `+`/`−` marker, content with
  4-column tab stops and visible control characters, full-width tint), wrap or clip with `‹`/`›`, edit cards,
  workspace `/diff` rendering and review-panel rows. `highlight.rs`: line-based lexical highlighter by extension.
  `theme.rs`: colour-depth detection and frame downsampling.
- **Transcript**: a successful edit's tool row becomes a card `✓ Edited path  +a −r` with up to 14 diff lines, hunk
  gaps (`⋯ N unchanged lines`), and an omission line with the exact count and the control that opens it
  (`… 48 more lines in 1 more hunk · ctrl+d to review`; `enter to review` when selected). Omission lines wrap rather
  than clip. A blank row separates cards from neighbouring operations. Repeated `file.diff` events replace their card;
  a failed edit never carries one.
- **Review panel** (ctrl+d, or enter on a selected edit or `/diff` output): `Edit diff · this operation only` with
  `edit k of N`, or `Workspace diff · unstaged changes to tracked files (git diff)`; `n`/`p` hunks, `]`/`[` edits (or
  files), scrolling, `←`/`→` panning, `w` wrap, `i` the call record; esc returns with the transcript position and the
  draft unchanged. Discloses when the shown diff is cut and names the complete file.
- **Sidecar**: git-exact missing-final-newline markers (previously a vague "(one side)" line, and a change of only the
  final newline produced an empty diff); control characters in diffs made visible instead of stripped; `diff_lines`,
  `hunks`, `full_path` on `file.diff`; `diff_chars`, `diff_path` on `tool.detail`; every operation's complete redacted
  diff written to `~/.nexus/sessions/<session>.diffs/` (0600) and served from disk after the in-memory record is
  dropped; `/diff` runs `git diff --no-color`.
- **Stability**: while scrolled back, the window stays anchored on its top row as cards arrive or grow below it.
  `SidecarMsg::Event` is boxed (clippy `large_enum_variant` after the new fields).

## Tests actually run

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `make build` | pass |
| `make test` (main working tree, before commit) | Rust 219/219, CLI 722/722, security gates pass |
| `cargo test --release --bin nexus-tui` (after the final lint fix) | 202/202 |
| `cargo clippy --release --bin nexus-tui --tests` | 0 warnings in `src/bin/nexus_tui/` (21 pre-existing warnings elsewhere in `harness-core`) |
| `NEXUS_E2E_EVIDENCE=1 tsx --test test/tui_diff_e2e.test.ts` in a clean worktree of `35ef104` | pass |

New regression tests: parser line numbers and header-like lines inside hunks; git headers (rename, binary, new,
deleted, no-eol, cut marker); exact row width, gutter alignment and tints; wide characters wrapping and clipping;
control characters never drawn; card bounding and exact omission counts; path elision; WCAG ≥ 4.5:1 for every syntax
and marker colour on every row background (24-bit and 256); colour-depth detection and downsampling; one card per
edit and replacement on repeat; failed edit never shows a change; alignment at 40/60/120 columns; ctrl+d review with
limit disclosure, hunk jump and draft/position kept; panning and wrap; anchoring while diffs arrive; 256/16/mono
rendering; sidecar no-eol markers, hunk counts, visible controls, on-disk complete diff and retrieval after eviction.

The PTY scenario (real `nexus-tui --live` + real sidecar + mock gateway) covers: multi-hunk mixed edit, repeated
edit, failed edit, new file, deletion, long path with a long line, tabs, Unicode/CJK, blank lines, missing final
newline, a 240-line change, OSC 52 and screen-clear sequences in file content, an uncommitted operator change made
before the turn (never attributed to the agent), resize to 72×30 and back while edits arrive, steering while busy
(queued then applied once), zero bytes drawn while idle, review navigation and return, `/diff` and its review, and
separate 256-colour, 16-colour and monochrome sessions.

## Shell-command coverage

Per-operation diffs cover the file-edit tools (`write_file`, `edit_file`, `patch_file`, `delete_file`). Changes made
by shell commands (`run_command`, `!command`) get no per-operation diff; they are visible only in `/diff`.

## Remaining limitations

- Syntax highlighting is lexical and per line: a block comment or string spanning lines is coloured only on its
  opening line (continuations starting with `*` are recognised). Unknown extensions stay plain.
- No edit tool renames files, so renames appear only in `/diff` when git reports them.
- `/diff` is `git diff`: staged changes and untracked files are not included (the label says so).
- 16-colour mode uses only the 16 standard colours, but crossterm encodes them as `38;5;0–15`; a terminal that cannot
  parse that SGR form at all is not supported (true for the whole TUI, not new).
- 256-colour row tints (palette 22/52) are more saturated than the 24-bit ones; contrast is still ≥ 4.5:1.
- Hunk navigation cannot move a hunk to the top of the panel when the rest of the diff is shorter than the panel
  (the panel never scrolls past its end); the hunk is still in view.
- An approval request replaces an open review panel; it must be reopened afterwards.
- Emoji with variation selectors may measure differently in some terminals (unicode-width rules).

## Visual acceptance

Inspected in the rendered screenshots, after fixing what the first passes showed (stale binary, a heading repeated
in the review panel, transcript bleeding beside the panel, the gutter bar touching the border, a path broken
mid-name, an omission hint clipped at 72 columns, an overstated workspace label): hierarchy (status glyph, verb, dimmed
directory, bold file name, coloured counts) reads at a glance; rows align at every width tested; tints are muted and
span the row; syntax colours stay legible on them; density is bounded by the 14-line preview; navigation is labelled
in the panel footer and the omission line. **Verdict: accepted by my own visual inspection of the captured run;
independent review pending.**

fix(doctor): --deep engine probe no longer fails in large workspaces

The engine.tool check listed the workspace recursively and parsed the output,
but the doctor's process runner keeps only the first 64 KB of stdout. In a home
directory workspace the listing was 812 KB (6,715 entries), so the cut JSON did
not parse and a working engine was reported as "could not execute a read-only
tool". The probe now lists one level (max_depth 1) and keeps up to 16 MB of
output for that call. Regression test: a workspace whose listing exceeds 64 KB.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

<pasted_content id="ac96">
Bring the rest of Nexus’s live TUI to the same visual maturity standard as the improved diff presentation. Implement and validate the interface beyond diffs: transcript, composer, activity/status, tools, commands, navigation, panels, approvals, errors, and session recovery.

Read applicable AGENTS.md instructions and inspect the actual checkout. Preserve unrelated work and integrate with the existing diff components and theme. No reference screenshots are available on this server; use the criteria below.

Start by running the TUI and identifying concrete visual and interaction defects. Save a concise acceptance matrix, then implement the improvements. Do not stop at an audit, proposal, or theme change.

1. Consistent hierarchy and layout
Use coherent spacing, alignment, typography emphasis, gutters, colors, and panel boundaries. Clearly distinguish user messages, assistant responses, tool activity, notices, and terminal outcomes. Keep file paths, commands, and technical details readable without overwhelming the conversation. Avoid redundant banners and repeated status information.

2. Readable transcript
Render paragraphs, lists, headings, code blocks, and supported tables consistently. Preserve code indentation and provide inspectable handling for long lines. Bound large tool output with explicit omission counts and access to complete evidence. Keep streaming text stable without duplicating content or exposing partial formatting artifacts.

Preserve the reader’s scroll position when new output arrives. Follow live output when already at the bottom; otherwise show a clear new-output indicator and a discoverable way to return.

3. Polished composer
Make focus, cursor position, multiline editing, paste buffers, and submission behavior clear. Support long drafts without consuming the whole screen. Keep editing usable during active work, and distinguish ordinary submission from steering.

Provide discoverable controls for newline insertion, paste inspection/editing/removal, history, and cancellation. Preserve drafts when opening panels or recovering from errors. Show queued, applied, rejected, and undelivered steering accurately.

4. Activity and status
Present a compact animated activity indicator with useful phase and elapsed time. Distinguish inference, tool execution, compaction, verification, provider wait, approval wait, and cancellation.

Keep model, workspace, branch, and session information identifiable without crowding narrow terminals. Display continuation/budget information when relevant. Never leave an active-looking indicator after completion or failure, or imply progress when the process is disconnected.

5. Tool presentation
Use concise tool headers with meaningful subjects, accurate running/succeeded/failed/cancelled states, and appropriate duration information. Separate explanation from command output and evidence.

Provide consistent expandable details and scrolling. Do not present empty output, failed operations, or unavailable evidence as success. Preserve the improved diff presentation for edits.

6. Commands and navigation
Make slash-command completion, filtering, selection, descriptions, and argument hints usable by keyboard. Keep help and completion synchronized with supported commands; obsolete commands must not reappear.

Use predictable focus and escape behavior across menus and panels. Provide visible shortcuts appropriate to the current context. Opening and closing views must preserve transcript position and composer state.

7. Approvals and consequential actions
Show what is proposed, the affected target, and the available decisions clearly. Keep approval controls distinct from ordinary composer submission. Make keyboard focus and the selected decision unambiguous.

Prevent accidental acceptance from buffered input or paste. Explain pending approvals and repair busy-state limitations without burying them in tool output.

8. Errors, outcomes, and recovery
Present concise errors with the useful cause, current state, and next action. Make detailed diagnostics accessible separately.

Clearly distinguish execution completion, verification success/failure, incomplete requirements, bounded termination, interruption, and disconnection. Avoid conflicting success banners and failure messages.

Provide understandable startup, empty-session, resume, crash, reconnect, and recovery states. Preserve user text and identify undelivered input. Recovery controls must reflect actions the runtime actually supports.

9. Terminal robustness and accessibility
Test wide, narrow, and short windows, resizing during streaming, Unicode display width, combining characters, emoji, tabs, and long paths. Layout must degrade gracefully without overlapping controls or hiding essential input/status.

Use readable contrast, limited-color and monochrome fallbacks, and text/symbol cues beyond color. Escape untrusted terminal control sequences. Maintain compatibility with supported terminal environments and keyboard behavior.

10. Rendering performance
Avoid flicker, excessive full-screen redraws, stale rows, scroll jumps, and input latency. Idle state should not redraw unnecessarily. Keep large transcripts and output panels bounded or virtualized without losing access to evidence.

Use shared components and theme tokens. Preserve runtime semantics; identify any backend change required for truthful presentation and test it explicitly. Do not expand this work into unrelated inference or compaction redesign.

Validation:
- Exercise the real TUI and sidecar through a pseudo-terminal.
- Cover startup, streaming, slow inference, tool success/failure, edits, steering, multiline paste, approvals, cancellation, compaction, verification failure, incomplete requirements, disconnection, and resume.
- Test keyboard-only navigation, drafts, scroll preservation, narrow layouts, and resizing during active work.
- Add meaningful regression checks for layout, focus, escaping, state transitions, and duplicate output.
- Run required builds and relevant tests.
- Capture representative terminal screenshots and a recording with monotonic timestamps, tied to the tested commit/build.
- Independently inspect the rendered artifacts. Correct visible defects rather than relying solely on passing tests.

Finish with the acceptance matrix, changes, tested commit/build identity, tests actually run, representative visual evidence, remaining limitations, and a clear accepted/blocked verdict. Do not publish or deploy.
</pasted_content id="ac96">

"""Drives the real `nexus-tui --live` (with the real sidecar) through the whole interface, not only diffs: startup,
streamed Markdown, slow inference, tool success and failure, large command output, an edit, steering, a multi-line
paste, an approval in review mode (with buffered keys), cancellation, compaction, a verification failure, incomplete
requirements, scroll preservation while output arrives, slash completion and help, narrow and short windows with
resizing during work, a sidecar crash and restart, and resuming the saved session.

It captures named screens (cells with colours, rendered to PNG by render_screens.py) and prints a JSON summary; the
node test (tui_surface_e2e.test.ts) owns the mock gateway and asserts on the summary and the sidecar logs.

Usage: tui_surface_driver.py PLAN.json
"""
import json
import os
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from tui_diff_driver import DiffSession, has  # noqa: E402
from tui_pty_driver import T0, count_events, wait_events  # noqa: E402


def children(pid):
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["pgrep", "-P", str(pid)], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        return [int(p) for p in out.split()]
    except Exception:
        return []


def main():
    plan = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
    env = dict(os.environ, **plan["env"])
    events = plan["env"]["NEXUS_RECORD_EVENTS"]
    cast, shots, result = [], [], {}
    argv = [plan["tui"], "--live", "--sidecar", plan["recorder"], "--node", plan["node"], "--"] + plan["sidecar_args"]
    turns = lambda: count_events(events, "turn.result")  # noqa: E731

    def shot(session, name):
        shots.append(session.color.snapshot(name))
        result.setdefault("screens", {})[name] = session.color.lines()

    s = DiffSession(argv, env, 120, 36, cast)
    s.wait_text("enter send", 30)
    s.pump(0.4)
    shot(s, "01-startup")

    # Streamed Markdown; scroll back while it streams, then return.
    s.send("Explain the plan for the cache layer.\r", settle=0.1)
    s.wait_screen(lambda lines: has(lines, "Cache layer plan"), 15, "streamed heading")
    s.pump(0.6)
    shot(s, "02-streaming")
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 1, 30, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    s.pump(0.3)
    shot(s, "03-markdown-final")

    # Slow inference, then tools: read, failed read, large command output, an edit; steering while busy.
    s.send("Inspect the repository and add the cache module.\r", settle=0.1)
    s.pump(1.2)
    shot(s, "04-slow-inference")
    s.send("prefer an LRU policy\r", settle=0.2)
    s.pump(0.3)
    shot(s, "05-steering-queued")
    # Scroll back while output keeps arriving.
    s.send("\x1b[5~", settle=0.3)
    before_scroll = s.color.lines()[1:-3]
    wait_events(events, "tool.end", 3, 30, s)
    s.pump(0.5)
    result["scroll_kept"] = s.color.lines()[1:-3] == before_scroll
    shot(s, "06-scrolled-back-new-output")
    s.send("\x1b[6~" * 8, settle=0.3)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 2, 60, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    s.pump(0.3)
    shot(s, "07-tools-final")

    # A multi-line paste, inspected, then sent.
    s.send("\x1b[200~line one of the note\r\n\tindented line ✓ 字\r\nline three\x1b[201~", settle=0.4)
    shot(s, "08-paste-buffer")
    s.send("\x0f", settle=0.4)  # ctrl+o
    shot(s, "09-paste-view")
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.3)
    s.send("\r", settle=0.2)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 3, 30, s)
    s.wait_idle()

    # Review mode: an approval; keys typed just before it opens must not answer it.
    s.send("/mode review\r", settle=0.5)
    s.send("Write the config file.\r", settle=0.05)
    s.send("yyy", settle=0.05)
    s.wait_screen(lambda lines: has(lines, "Approval needed"), 20, "the approval modal")
    s.pump(0.5)
    shot(s, "10-approval")
    result["approval_survived_buffered_keys"] = has(s.color.lines(), "Approval needed")
    s.send("y", settle=0.4)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 4, 30, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    s.send("/mode auto\r", settle=0.5)

    # Cancellation during a slow step.
    s.send("Take a long time on this.\r", settle=0.1)
    s.pump(1.5)
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.1)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 5, 30, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    s.pump(0.3)
    shot(s, "11-cancelled")

    # Compaction.
    s.send("/compact\r", settle=0.3)
    s.wait_screen(lambda lines: has(lines, "ompact"), 20, "compaction output")
    s.pump(0.6)
    s.wait_idle()
    shot(s, "12-compacted")

    # A verification failure: an edit, then the repository's failing test command.
    s.send("Fix the parser bug.\r", settle=0.2)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 6, 120, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    s.pump(0.4)
    shot(s, "13-verification-failed")

    # Incomplete requirements (numbered list typed with shift-less newlines via alt+enter).
    s.send("Do these:\x1b\r1. add a README section\x1b\r2. add a changelog entry", settle=0.3)
    s.send("\r", settle=0.2)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 7, 60, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    s.pump(0.4)
    shot(s, "14-requirements-incomplete")

    # Slash completion and help, with a draft kept.
    s.send("/re", settle=0.4)
    shot(s, "15-completion")
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.2)
    s.send("\x0c", settle=0.2)  # ctrl+l clears the draft
    s.send("a draft I am keeping", settle=0.2)
    s.send("\t", settle=0.2)  # transcript focus
    s.send("[", settle=0.3)
    shot(s, "16-transcript-focus")
    s.send("\r", settle=0.6)
    shot(s, "17-tool-detail")
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.3)
    s.send("\t", settle=0.2)
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.2)
    s.send("\x15", settle=0.1)  # ctrl+u: clear the line so ? opens help
    s.send("?", settle=0.4)
    shot(s, "18-help")
    s.send("\x1b", settle=0.3)

    # Narrow and short windows; resize while a turn streams.
    s.set_size(60, 24)
    s.pump(0.5)
    shot(s, "19-narrow")
    s.set_size(80, 12)
    s.pump(0.5)
    shot(s, "20-short")
    s.set_size(120, 36)
    s.pump(0.4)
    s.send("Stream another answer.\r", settle=0.1)
    s.pump(0.6)
    s.set_size(64, 24)
    s.pump(0.5)
    shot(s, "21-resize-during-stream")
    s.set_size(120, 36)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 8, 30, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    s.pump(0.3)

    # Idle: nothing redrawn.
    before = len(s.raw)
    s.pump(2.0)
    result["idle_bytes"] = len(s.raw) - before

    # The sidecar dies: the crash screen, then restart.
    s.send("a draft before the crash", settle=0.2)
    for child in children(s.pid):
        os.kill(child, signal.SIGKILL)
    s.wait_screen(lambda lines: has(lines, "stopped"), 15, "the crash screen")
    s.pump(0.5)
    shot(s, "22-crashed")
    s.send("r", settle=0.3)
    s.wait_text("enter send", 30)
    s.pump(0.5)
    shot(s, "23-restarted")
    s.send("\x03", settle=0.1)
    s.send("\x03", settle=0.1)
    result["first_exit"] = s.wait_exit(20)

    # Resume the saved session.
    cast.append([round(time.monotonic() - T0, 4), "m", "new TUI process: resume the saved session (-r latest)"])
    r = DiffSession(argv + ["-r", "latest"], env, 120, 36, cast)
    r.wait_text("Resumed session", 30)
    r.wait_idle()
    r.pump(0.4)
    shot(r, "24-resumed")
    r.send("\x03", settle=0.1)
    result["second_exit"] = r.wait_exit(20)

    times = [frame[0] for frame in cast]
    result["recording"] = {"frames": len(cast), "monotonic": all(b >= a for a, b in zip(times, times[1:])), "duration_s": times[-1] if times else 0}
    result["raw_has_file_escape"] = "\x1b]52;" in (s.raw + r.raw).decode("utf-8", "replace")
    with open(plan["cast"], "w") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({"version": 2, "width": 120, "height": 36, "timestamp": int(time.time()), "env": {"TERM": env.get("TERM", "")}}) + "\n")
        for frame in cast:
            f.write(json.dumps(frame) + "\n")
    with open(plan["screens"], "w") as f:
        json.dump(shots, f)
    print(json.dumps(result))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 7, 60, s)

    s.pump(0.4)

content.thinking: The logs confirm "yyy" stayed correctly in the draft rather than being treated as approval — the real issue was my driver appending "/mode auto" to that draft before submitting. I'll clear the draft first to fix this.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='cli/test/helpers/tui_surface_driver.py'
s=open(p).read()
old='''    s.send("y", settle=0.4)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 4, 30, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    s.send("/mode auto\\r", settle=0.5)'''
new='''    s.send("y", settle=0.4)
    wait_events(events, "turn.result", 4, 30, s)
    s.wait_idle()
    result["draft_after_approval"] = s.color.lines()[-1]
    s.send("\\x0c", settle=0.2)  # the buffered keys stayed in the draft: clear it
    s.send("/mode auto\\r", settle=0.5)'''
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cd cli && NEXUS_E2E_EVIDENCE=1 NEXUS_SURFACE_AUDIT=1 npx tsx --test test/tui_surface_e2e.test.ts 2>&1 | grep -E "^ℹ (pass|fail)|AssertionError|Error:|never" -A3 | head -30

# Live TUI surface maturity — acceptance matrix (2026-10-12)

Request: bring the rest of the live TUI (transcript, composer, activity/status, tools, commands, navigation, panels,
approvals, errors, recovery) to the standard of the diff presentation, validated through the real TUI and sidecar.

Baseline: commit `3727938`, captured by `cli/test/tui_surface_e2e.test.ts` (audit mode) into
`docs/reviews/evidence/tui_surface_baseline/` (24 screens, recording, sidecar logs). Status is filled in at the end
of the work; a row is only `PASS` when the final PTY run (or a named regression test) shows it.

| # | Area | Defect observed in the baseline (screen) | Acceptance criterion | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Transcript | Markdown shown raw: `##`, `**`, backticks, ``` fences, table pipes (03) | Headings, emphasis, inline code, lists with hanging indents, fenced code in a gutter block with syntax colour and wrapped long lines, aligned tables; no marker characters left over | |
| 2 | Transcript | Three model replies of one turn concatenated without a break: "Both items are handled.Both items…" (14) | Each model reply is its own paragraph; nothing duplicated or run together | |
| 3 | Streaming | Partial lines show raw markers while streaming (02) | Unclosed formatting on the streaming line is not shown as literal markers; text does not reflow into duplicates | |
| 4 | Outcomes | Banners dump enums: `TURN ENDED - UNVERIFIED execution=COMPLETED outcome=UNVERIFIED (VERIFICATION_NOT_RUN)`; interrupt adds "0 tool call(s) not dispatched" (07, 11) | One line naming the outcome in words (done / verified / not verified / verification failed / requirements open / cancelled / stopped at a limit / model request failed), a short cause and the next action; raw fields only in the receipt (v) | |
| 5 | Outcomes | Requirements banner repeats itself in a second "Objective incomplete" info line and omits the requirement text (14) | Remaining requirements listed once, with their text | |
| 6 | Tools | Command output is not shown at all; success of `seq 1 120` gives no line count; the tool summary sent for commands is `{` (07, events) | Bounded output preview (stdout/stderr, exit code) with an exact omission count and the control that opens the full record; empty output says so; failures never look like success | |
| 7 | Tools | No durations | Duration on finished tools that took noticeable time; live elapsed on long running ones | |
| 8 | Status | Two spinners while busy: status bar and composer line (02, 04) | One activity indicator (composer line) with phase, elapsed, step/segment and the cancel key; the status bar shows identity only | |
| 9 | Status | Model and mode are bare words ("m auto"); crowded at narrow widths (19) | Labelled, prioritised segments that drop the least important first on narrow terminals; review mode visible | |
| 10 | Scrolling | Scrolled back, the badge says "18 more rows" but not that new output arrived; End in the composer does not return | Position kept while output arrives (baseline already keeps it); badge says new output arrived and names how to return (pgdn, ctrl+end) | |
| 11 | Composer | Pasted prompt appears in the transcript only as `[Pasted text #1: 3 lines]` (08) | The submitted text is shown (bounded, with omission count) | |
| 12 | Composer | No placeholder; long drafts give no sign of hidden lines | Placeholder naming send/steer/help; a line indicator when the draft is taller than the composer | |
| 13 | Approvals | Modal leaves transcript text visible in its margins; file changes use the old plain diff colouring; decisions only in the border (10) | Full panel, target and kind stated, diffs rendered with the shared diff component, decision buttons with a visible focus; buffered keys and pastes cannot decide (baseline: grace period holds) | |
| 14 | Panels | Help and other centred panels show cut transcript text beside them; long help lines are cut (18) | Panels clear what is behind them; help text wraps | |
| 15 | Completion | Long descriptions cut without an ellipsis; no position in the list (15) | Ellipsis on cut text and `n/m` position; list comes only from the sidecar's commands | |
| 16 | Crash | 24 lines of spinner progress as "diagnostics"; "(no exit code)" for a signal (22) | Spinner/progress noise filtered, a few relevant lines kept; the signal named; the draft kept and recovery steps that the runtime supports (restart, then /resume) | |
| 17 | Resume | The resumed session shows only "Resumed session … (22 messages)" over an empty transcript (24) | The earlier conversation (recent messages, bounded) is shown under a resumed-session divider | |
| 18 | Verification | Not reached in the baseline (the mock never called task_completed) | Verification failure shown as its own outcome with the failed command | |
| 19 | Robustness | — | Narrow (60), short (12 rows), resize while streaming, CJK/emoji/combining marks, tabs, long paths, escapes in output: no overlap, essential input/status kept, no control sequence emitted | |
| 20 | Performance | Idle draws 0 bytes, scroll kept (baseline PASS) | Still 0 bytes idle; no duplicate entries | |
